memos.risk:
Risk officer view: I'd refuse a buy here, at any size.

Reasons, from the brief:
- The first two minutes after graduation show a launch bot present, top-5 buyers holding 86% of early buys, and a sell-to-buy ratio near 0.96. That pattern points to coordinated early flow, not organic demand.
- Bundle share is 27% and top-3 holders control 19% of the curve, so supply is concentrated.
- Last 15 minutes: net flow is essentially flat (+0.05 SOL) on 74 SOL of volume, with 49 sellers against 82 buyers. Churn, not accumulation.
- The coin is already 38% off its 30-minute high, and the name is a slur-based token with a recognizable meme. Treat it as data, but it signals hype-chasing and attention decay.
- Pool depth of 125 SOL means a $20 round trip eats most of the 1.4-5.1% cost band before any move.

If the desk ever overrode this, the cap would be $5, a 20% stop, and a 15-minute hold. But the base rates and the flow profile don't justify the override. Skip it.
memos.scout:
The strongest honest case: this is classified ORGANIC, with no airdrop dump seen and 111 curve buyers, and the coin is still up 115% over 30 minutes. Buyer breadth is decent, and top-3 curve share is only 19%, so no single wallet dominates the curve. Last 15 minutes show 82 buyers against 49 sellers, with 74 SOL bought, so demand has not fully vanished, and the pool holds 125 SOL of depth, enough that a $20 ticket won't move price much.

But the case is weak. Net flow over the last 15 minutes is essentially flat (0.05 SOL), the sell-to-buy ratio at graduation was 0.96, and the first two minutes were dominated by a launch bot and a top-5 buyer share of 86%. The coin is already 38% off its 30-minute high, and the recent return is negative. Demand is being absorbed by sellers rather than building. Against a roughly 20% base-rate loss on random post-graduation buys and round-trip costs of 1.4-5.1%, nothing here shows that demand will persist for the next 30-60 minutes. My recommendation is to skip.
memos.skeptic: The most likely way this loses money is a slow insider distribution after a 38% drawdown from the 30-minute high. The first 2 minutes after graduation show top-5 buyers holding 85.5% of early buys, a 0.96 sell-to-buy ratio, and a launch bot present, which points to coordinated early wallets now exiting. Over the last 15 minutes, 74.2 SOL was sold against 74.2 SOL bought, with net flow of just 0.05 SOL and a -2.5% return, so the market is absorbing sells without any real bid. The curve shows a 26.8% bundle share and 39.6% completer share, consistent with insiders still holding. With a 125 SOL pool, a $20 ticket faces roughly 1.4-5.1% round-trip costs, and a flat-to-down drift would eat that before any bounce. Skip.
